title: Redwood Discovery: Model selection - Bluehelm MedTech
next_steps: Send hosted vs dedicated pricing + commitment tiers
Share SOC 2 and security pack (SSO, KMS, audit logs)
Schedule 1-week benchmark run on 32k context model (Devon + Jenny)

summary: Initial discovery to scope model selection for NER + clinical note summarization and a patient-facing multilingual assistant. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for latency and compliance. Key needs: 32k+ context for long notes, tool-calling for EHR lookups, Spanish + Mandarin support, SOC2/KMS/SSO. Agreed next steps: send pricing + security docs, schedule benchmark with sample notes.
topics: tool-calling / function calling for EHR queries
hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC, on-prem)
latency vs cost tradeoffs and batching/caching
security requirements: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-24
Time: 14:00 - 14:45 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Ortiz (Redwood AE), Devon Liu (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (Head of ML, Bluehelm), Marcus Lee (CTO), Jenny Park (Data Eng)

[00:00] Samantha Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'm Samantha with Redwood, AE on the account. we also have Devon our solutions engineer. how's everybody doing?
[00:08] Dr. Priya Rao: Hi Samantha, good thanks. we've got about 45 minutes, hope that's ok.
[00:12] Marcus Lee: Morning all. quick note we are in san francisco so apologies if i'm a little late to the timezone math.
[00:18] Samantha Ortiz: no worries. quick agenda: 1) understand your current stack and workloads, 2) model selection needs — context length, multilingual, tool-calling — and 3) constraints: security, latency, budget. then we can decide next steps. sound ok?
[00:29] Marcus Lee: sounds great.
[00:31] Jenny Park: yep.

--- Discovery / current stack ---
[00:35] Devon Liu: quick question — what are you using today for models / inference?
[00:38] Dr. Priya Rao: we're primarily using OpenAI's API for prototyping, and a mix of a small internal Llama-based self-hosted endpoint for some batch tasks. For clinical NER and note summarization we currently post-process with rules, but it's getting messy. latency for the patient-facing assistant needs to be under ~1s for short queries but for long summarization jobs we can tolerate more.
[01:02] Samantha Ortiz: ok. and what's the volume like? tokens per month, typical QPS?
[01:06] Marcus Lee: currently low — maybe 5k requests/month but a few hundred embeddings calls. pilot could push to tens of thousands of requests monthly. QPS spikes will be short but we want predictable tail latency.
[01:18] Devon Liu: got it. do you plan to host PHI on the platform or keep data in your environment?
[01:23] Jenny Park: yes, PHI will touch the models for summarization. we need either dedicated isolated capacity or a private deployment. SOC2 + KMS + SSO are must-haves.
[01:33] Samantha Ortiz: understood — so Hosted API might work for initial prototyping, but Dedicated or Private will be likely for production with PHI.

--- Model requirements: context length ---
[01:40] Samantha Ortiz: talk to me about context length — you mentioned long clinical notes?
[01:44] Dr. Priya Rao: our notes can be very long, often 10k to 20k tokens per patient encounter, with attachments and historical context pushing some to 30k+. For summarization we want a single-pass summary across the full note and prior notes, so 32k context would be ideal, 64k is a nice-to-have but not required initially.
[02:05] Devon Liu: okay so we're looking at models and variants that support 32k. we also need to consider quantization and perf: larger context increases memory and latency. are you targeting CPU or GPU?
[02:16] Marcus Lee: GPU, likely A10 or A100 for Dedicated. cost is a concern.
[02:21] Jenny Park: also important: we plan to do embeddings for search across notes — we prefer to keep embedding compute co-located to avoid egress and latency.

--- Multilingual needs ---
[02:30] Samantha Ortiz: multilingual — what languages and use cases?
[02:32] Dr. Priya Rao: Spanish is top priority for patient communications, and a smaller Mandarin-speaking cohort. Accuracy for medical terminology in translations and summaries is critical.
[02:43] Devon Liu: some open models handle multilingual well but vary by domain. we can run benchmarks for Spanish/medical terms; also there are fine-tune or retrieval-augmented approaches to help.

--- Tool-calling / function-calling ---
[02:53] Samantha Ortiz: you mentioned tool-calling for EHR lookups — can you describe flows?
[02:57] Jenny Park: user asks assistant 'what meds has patient X been prescribed in the last year' — assistant should call a function to query EHR, then synthesize the answer and cite. We need secure function calls (no leaking credentials), and audit logs for function call events.
[03:15] Devon Liu: Redwood supports function/tool calling patterns and structured outputs — can do direct calls to customer APIs on Dedicated/Private to avoid sensitive data in the hosted plane, or use a secure connector. We log events per-request with trace ids.
[03:28] Marcus Lee: good. is function calling available on hosted tier today?
[03:31] Samantha Ortiz: yes, basic function calling is available on Hosted, but for PHI we typically recommend Dedicated or Private so that the calls and keys remain in your VPC or on-prem.

--- Security / compliance ---
[03:41] Dr. Priya Rao: our security team will require SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML, customer-managed KMS, audit logs retained 1 year, and fine-grained RBAC. Also data residency: EU for EU patients.
[03:56] Devon Liu: Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering, customer KMS integrations, and audit logs — we can also run an on-prem Private deployment for strict data residency. we have an enterprise security pack — i'll share the docs.
[04:10] Jenny Park: do you have experience with hospital integrations — FHIR connectors?
[04:14] Samantha Ortiz: yes, customers have implemented FHIR connectors via the secure connector pattern; we can point to an example architecture.

--- Latency, batching, caching, cost tradeoffs ---
[04:22] Marcus Lee: back to latency — short assistant queries need sub-1s p95. Summaries can be asynchronous. how do we control cost?
[04:30] Devon Liu: key levers: shorter context windows for interactive flows, prefix caching/kv cache for repeated context, and batching for throughput. For p95 <1s we can route interactive requests to low-latency nodes and use smaller models; for long summaries route to high-context models with longer tail latency. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching settings for your workload.
[04:50] Dr. Priya Rao: curious about 32k models' latency on A10 vs A100 — any rough numbers?
[04:55] Devon Liu: rough rule: A100 will be 2-3x faster for large context and higher throughput; A10 is cost-efficient at moderate loads. We can run a benchmark with your sample notes to give exact p50/p95.

--- Model comparisons and open models ---
[05:08] Samantha Ortiz: on models, are you considering open models only or hybrid with closed?
[05:11] Dr. Priya Rao: we'd prefer open models for reproducibility and to avoid vendor lock, but accuracy on medical terminology is top priority. open to curated weights if they perform well.
[05:21] Devon Liu: we recommend evaluating a few families: Llama 4 (32k variant), Mistral and open LLMs that have strong multilingual support, and some fine-tuned instruction models for clinical tasks. We'll include Redwood-verified perf profiles for each.
[05:36] Marcus Lee: what about hallucination in clinical summarization?
[05:39] Devon Liu: that comes down to prompt + retrieval + model. RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) using embeddings for source citation reduces hallucination, and function-calling to surface EHR facts helps. Also we have quality monitoring to detect regressions.

--- Pilot scope and success criteria ---
[05:58] Samantha Ortiz: what would success look like for a pilot?
[06:01] Dr. Priya Rao: 1) Summaries with >90% factual accuracy on a 100-sample audit, 2) p95 latency <1s for interactive flows, 3) Spanish summaries within 5% of English accuracy on key clinical terms, 4) security review passed.
[06:17] Marcus Lee: timeline — we'd like a pilot in Q1, 6-8 week POC.
[06:22] Samantha Ortiz: good — we can propose a Dedicated pilot with a 32k model profile and a Hosted fallback for prototyping.

--- Objections / tradeoffs (recorded imperfect transcriptions) ---
[06:30] Dr. Priya Rao: cost is, uh, the main blocker for us. we need to show unit economics.
[06:34] Samantha Ortiz: totally. we'll run a cost model: tokens, embeddings, inf time per request, and show options: token-limited hosted for prototyping, reserved Dedicated for committed throughput, or Private for on-prem with different pricing.
[06:47] Jenny Park: and the ops overhead — if we go Private we don't want to be reinventing infra. what's your support?
[06:52] Devon Liu: Redwood offers enterprise support and can run the Private control plane, and we have managed deployment options; we'll include an SOW for the pilot.

--- Deep-dive: function calling & audit logs ---
[07:02] Marcus Lee: we need to ensure function calls are auditable and can be replayed in case of incidents. request/response payloads must be retained per policy.
[07:11] Devon Liu: yes, on Dedicated/Private we can retain request/response logs in your retention store. we can pseudonymize PHI in transit and keep keys customer-managed. Hosted has limited retention controls so less ideal for PHI.
[07:26] Dr. Priya Rao: great. any gotchas with model variants and KV cache — we've seen references to KV cache but not sure implications.
[07:33] Devon Liu: KV cache is the transformer key/value attention cache — it's huge with long context. for very long notes we recommend memory-optimized instances and kernel selection tuned to the sequence length. this is why A100 matters for 32k.

--- Benchmark planning ---
[07:50] Samantha Ortiz: next step: schedule a benchmark. Jenny, can you share a small set of de-identified notes (20-50) and a Spanish subset?
[07:58] Jenny Park: yes, we can de-id and share. target next week?
[08:01] Samantha Ortiz: we'll coordinate — Devon will run against 32k and 8k variants on A10/A100 and share perf + accuracy.
[08:09] Devon Liu: i'll also include embedding throughput numbers and cost per 1k queries estimate.

--- Questions from customer ---
[08:15] Marcus Lee: does Redwood support model pinning and can we do canary rollouts?
[08:19] Samantha Ortiz: yes — model version pinning, canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies by route.
[08:25] Dr. Priya Rao: how about encryption at rest and customer KMS?
[08:28] Devon Liu: customer-managed KMS is supported on Dedicated and Private; encryption at rest is standard. we'll include specifics in the security pack.
[08:37] Jenny Park: and monitoring for quality regressions?
[08:40] Samantha Ortiz: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring with prompt sets/eval hooks and regression alerts.

--- Recap and explicit next steps ---
[08:48] Samantha Ortiz: quick recap: pilot scope = Dedicated pilot on A100 with 32k model for summarization + embeddings; run benchmarks on your de-identified notes; security docs + SOC2 pack will be sent; draft SOW for a 6-8 week pilot.
[08:59] Dr. Priya Rao: yes that's right. Marcus?
[09:01] Marcus Lee: sounds good. target Q1 pilot.
[09:03] Jenny Park: i'll get the de-id notes and share by Friday.
[09:06] Samantha Ortiz: perfect. i'll send pricing and security docs today, Devon will follow up to schedule the benchmark and include the perf matrix.

[09:12] Devon Liu: thanks everyone. i'll add one more thing — we'll include recommended quantization and batching settings and expected cost delta between A10/A100.
[09:20] Dr. Priya Rao: thanks.
[09:22] Samantha Ortiz: ok we'll wrap. thanks all for your time.

--- End of meeting notes (timestamps approximate) ---
[44:30] call ended
